evidence.note: Builds /app/test_align.py to compute S3/Ea/E2 locally on baseline heuristics before trusting any alignment — metric implementation established early.

Every candidate scored with exact S3 reporting Ea and E2_aligned separately (e.g. 'S3≈0.234235 (Ea=10620, E2=21206)'); score used as the accept/reject and stopping objective ('keep if better, restore best if worse').

Trusted Python scorer detects that exact_replace.cpp accepted moves on incorrect E2 deltas and overwrote the best with a worse alignment; agent recovers from backup — scorer guards against edge-set delta bugs in its own optimizers.
Validates output format ('well-formed'), checks full coverage (wc -l), and scores the reference alignment getting NC=1.0 + sensible S3≈0.248 — sanity-checks the metric implementation.
SANA reports S3≈0.557 for yeast; agent independently recomputes exact S3≈0.557 AND NC≈0.169, discovering NC fails — treats reported/passing score as necessary-but-scrutinized, not final.

reasoning: The agent implemented faithful S3 and NC scorers, ran them on every alignment (tracking Ea and E2_aligned distinctly), verified injectivity/coverage/format, and sanity-checked by scoring the reference (NC=1.0), satisfying all anchor-8 criteria. It exceeds 8 with tight-feedback-loop behaviors: its trusted scorer caught an edge-set delta bug in its own C++ optimizer (step 53) and independently re-verified SANA's reported score to expose an NC failure (step 88). It stops short of a pure 10 only because there is no explicit edge-case unit-testing of the scorer's denominator, so I place it at 9.
